principle: Lineage grammar preserves Italian editorial DNA; evidence-level fingerprints preserve the visible identity of the selected historical specimen. Prompt text is compiler output, never authority.

layout: Use one monumental central image as the page field; keep the composition vertically frontal and nearly full-cover; do not subdivide the cover into independent modules.
image: Use one confrontational figurative subject at monumental scale; preserve the strong centered silhouette and direct frontal presence; the subject is the argument, not an illustration inside a layout.
typography: Keep the publication/title band confined to the upper edge; use one extremely small, saturated red editorial intervention over the central subject; maintain extreme scale contrast between masthead and intervention.
density: Concentrate almost all visual mass in the single central subject; keep secondary information extremely sparse; preserve open peripheral breathing room rather than filling it with modules.
sequence: Establish the dominant image first, then let the tiny editorial intervention change how the image is read; do not turn the cover into a gallery or information dashboard.
emergence: Meaning should emerge from the hierarchy between monumental evidence and minimal editorial annotation, not from added diagrams or decorative systems.

transferable: The subject identity may change while preserving scale, crop, position and visual role.
Text content may change while preserving typographic scale, placement and hierarchy.
forbidden: No secondary photograph or inset image.
No unrelated geometric modules, circles, bars or diagrammatic ornaments.
No additional illustration competing with the dominant subject.
items.fidelityQuestion: Without reading the copy, is the result immediately recognizable as structurally descended from this selected cover?

layout: Preserve the specimen's dominant evidence field and restrained editorial framing; derive divisions from the observed cover rather than a generic modernist grid.
image: Treat the primary image as evidence with a single clear argumentative role; do not multiply image regions unless they are visible in the specimen.
typography: Preserve the observed title-to-image hierarchy and restrained secondary type; typography must annotate the evidence rather than become an unrelated graphic system.
density: Keep information density close to the specimen: one primary visual event, restrained secondary information and deliberate breathing room.
sequence: Let image, title and hierarchy form one editorial argument rather than a collection of modules.
emergence: Reveal the editorial position through the specimen's actual hierarchy, not through invented decoration.

transferable: Subject and copy may change only within the same visual roles.
forbidden: Do not invent additional image regions.
Do not draw a grid merely to signal modernism.
Do not add geometric accents absent from the selected specimen.
items.fidelityQuestion: Does the new work preserve the selected specimen's visible hierarchy before it expresses the broader Casabella lineage?

layout: Build the page from a dominant photographic field plus a narrow peripheral information zone; preserve strong asymmetry and the specimen's major vertical and horizontal divisions; allow one translucent block to intrude across the photographic field.
image: Use an extreme close-up photographic subject that exceeds the frame and dominates the page; preserve aggressive crop and monumental facial/object scale rather than reducing the subject to a conventional portrait.
typography: Use an oversized high-contrast serif headline that crosses structural regions; counterweight it with very small widely tracked editorial microtype in peripheral zones; preserve the large-to-tiny scale jump.
material: Keep monochrome or restrained photography against warm paper and a muted metallic-gold/translucent overlay; the overlay should feel printed and semi-transparent, not like a digital UI card.
density: Use one overwhelming visual mass with sparse but precise peripheral information; density comes from scale contrast, not from filling every region.
sequence: Read in this order: dominant photograph establishes the field; headline cuts across it; compact information anchors the edge; the inserted translucent field remains visibly distinct.
irony: Let the compact technical/editorial information sit against an emotionally oversized subject without explanatory decoration.
emergence: The information layer should appear as a persistent foreign-local object over the established photographic field, preserving its own geometry rather than dissolving into the image.

transferable: Subject identity may change while preserving extreme crop, scale and anchor.
Headline and microcopy may change while preserving typographic roles and spatial relationships.
forbidden: No conventional centered portrait with generous margins.
No decorative geometry that is not serving the observed overlay/division logic.
Do not collapse the large-serif/microtype contrast into one typographic scale.
items.fidelityQuestion: Does the result retain the selected issue's extreme crop, asymmetric field, cross-boundary headline and compact edge information at first glance?

layout: Preserve the selected study's local graphic systems and their exact hierarchy rather than replacing them with a generic editorial grid.
image: Keep photography, illustration or diagram in the roles visibly assigned by the specimen; do not homogenize them into one image treatment.
typography: Maintain multi-scale navigation and editorial hierarchy with clearly differentiated display, annotation and microtype roles.
material: Preserve print-aware color fields and surface relationships visible in the specimen.
density: High information density must remain navigable through scale, grouping and whitespace, not through simplification.
sequence: Allow local visual identities to remain distinct while a stable navigation system binds them.
irony: Preserve playful information relationships only where they are evidenced by the specimen.
emergence: Let information become image through accumulation and hierarchy without losing navigability.

transferable: Content may change while visual roles, grouping and hierarchy remain stable.
forbidden: Do not flatten all modules into one uniform style.
Do not invent decorative modules unrelated to information roles.
items.fidelityQuestion: Can the selected study still be recognized through hierarchy and module relationships after content replacement?
